title: Common infectious diseases
examples: What causes the spread of diseases like cholera?
How do vaccines help us prevent infections?
Can you explain the difference between bacterial and viral diseases?

explain.say: Today we will learn about some common infectious diseases. These diseases are caused by tiny living things called pathogens. A pathogen is anything that can cause illness in a host.
Malaria is a serious disease spread by mosquitoes. The parasite lives inside human blood cells. Mosquitoes bite an infected person and pass the parasite on.
Tuberculosis or TB is a bacterial infection. It often affects the lungs, making breathing difficult. It can spread through the air when an infected person coughs.
HIV attacks the immune system, making the body weak. It is transmitted through contact with certain body fluids. This weakens the body's ability to fight off infections.
Cholera is caused by contaminated water. Drinking water with cholera bacteria can lead to severe diarrhoea. This causes rapid dehydration if not treated.
To prevent these diseases, we must practice good hygiene. Washing hands often and ensuring clean water sources are very important steps. Vaccination is also a key prevention method.

faq.q: What is the difference between a virus and bacteria?
faq.a: Bacteria are single-celled living organisms that can often be treated with antibiotics. Viruses are much smaller and cannot reproduce on their own, needing a host cell to multiply.

faq.q: How long does it take for a disease to become contagious?
faq.a: The incubation period varies greatly depending on the pathogen and the disease. Some diseases can spread very quickly after exposure.
asks: How fast do I get sick?

faq.q: Are there any diseases that are only spread by air?
faq.a: Yes, diseases like tuberculosis are spread through droplets in the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes. This requires good ventilation.
asks: How do I avoid airborne germs?

faq.q: Why is clean water so important for preventing illness?
faq.a: Many pathogens, like the bacteria causing cholera, live in contaminated water sources. Boiling or filtering water removes these harmful germs.
asks: How do I make water safe?

faq.q: Does getting vaccinated give you permanent immunity?
faq.a: Vaccines train your immune system to recognize and fight specific pathogens. While protection can wane, boosters can help maintain that immunity.

facts: Malaria is transmitted through the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis and primarily affects the lungs.
Cholera is a severe diarrhoeal illness caused by ingesting contaminated water or food.
HIV attacks the immune system by targeting CD4 T-cells, weakening the body's defenses.

quiz.say: Which disease is spread through contaminated water?
quiz.why: Cholera is specifically linked to ingesting water contaminated with bacteria.

wrong.0: Malaria is spread by mosquito bites, not contaminated water.
wrong.1: TB is spread through the air via respiratory droplets.
wrong.2: HIV is spread through specific body fluids, not typically through drinking water.

quiz.say: If a person coughs with TB, how is it most likely spread?
quiz.why: Coughing releases tiny particles containing the bacteria into the air.

wrong.0: While some diseases use this, TB is primarily respiratory.
wrong.2: Mosquito bites are the vector for diseases like malaria.
wrong.3: Waterborne diseases like cholera are spread through ingesting germs.

quiz.say: Preventing malaria requires avoiding mosquito bites. What is the best way to prevent this?
quiz.why: These methods physically block the mosquito from biting you.

wrong.0: Boiling water prevents waterborne diseases, not mosquito-borne ones.
wrong.1: While vaccines are key, prevention also involves physical barriers against the vector.
wrong.2: Handwashing prevents contact transmission, but not mosquito bites.
